'''Judy Franz''' (born 1938) is an American [[physicist]], educator and the former executive officer of the [[American Physical Society]].

==Biography==
The daughter of two chemists, Ruth Comroe and Eugene Rosenbaum, she grew up in Lansdowne, Pennsylvania. She received her B.A in physics in 1959 from [[Cornell University]] and pursued graduate studies in physics at the [[University of Illinois at Urbana–Champaign|University of Illinois]] where she earned a master's degree in 1961 and a Ph.D. in 1965.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://cwp.library.ucla.edu/Phase2/Franz,_Judy_R.@921234567.html#sip|title=Judy R. Franz|website=CWP at UCLA}}</ref><ref name="CSWP article">{{cite journal|title=Judy Franz Named Executive Officer of APS|journal=CSWP|date=Spring 1994|volume=14|issue=1|pages=1, 20, 21|url=http://www.aps.org/programs/women/reports/gazette/upload/spring94.pdf#zoom=100}}</ref> Shortly after earning her Ph.D., she worked as a post-doctoral fellow at the [[IBM]] research laboratory in [[Zurich, Switzerland]] from 1965 to 1967, before returning to America to serve as a physics professor at [[Indiana University]] for 18 years.<ref name="CSWP article"/> After her time at Indiana University, Franz spent 5 years on the faculty of [[West Virginia University]] and three years on the faculty of the [[University of Alabama Huntsville|University of Alabama in Huntsville]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url = https://engineering.illinois.edu/engage/distinguished-alumni-and-friends/distinguished/article/5658|title = University of Illinois Distinguished Alumni Awards: Judy R. Franz|date = 1997|access-date = 2015-04-16|website = Engineering at Illinois}}</ref> In 1994, she took a five-year leave of absence from her faculty position to assume her position as executive officer of the [[American Physical Society]] (APS).<ref name=":0" />

Franz has published a number of high-profile articles on [[condensed matter physics]],<ref>{{Cite journal|title = Excited-State Mixing in the Optical Pumping of Alkali-Metal Vapors|date = August 5, 1966|journal = Physical Review Letters|volume = 148|issue = 1|pages = 82–89|doi = 10.1103/PhysRev.148.82|bibcode = 1966PhRv..148...82F |last1 = Franz|first1 = Frank A.|last2 = Franz|first2 = Judy R.}}</ref> most notably related to the theoretical calculations of electron state [[wave function]]s in systems undergoing [[Metal–insulator transition|metal-insulator transitions]].<ref>{{Cite journal|title = Theory of metal-non-metal transitions in liquid-metal alloys|last = Franz|first = JR|date = February 1980|journal = Journal of Physics F: Metal Physics|volume = 10|issue = 2|pages = 235–252|doi = 10.1088/0305-4608/10/2/012|bibcode = 1980JPhF...10..235F }}</ref> She was a key advocate for improving [[physics education]], and has received the [[Melba Newell Phillips]] Medal for Creative Leadership in Physics Education from the [[American Association of Physics Teachers]].<ref name="phillips medal">{{cite web|title=Franz Awarded Phillips Medal|url=http://www.aapt.org/aboutaapt/Franz_Awarded_Phillips_Medal.cfm|website=American Association of Physics Teachers|access-date=14 January 2015}}</ref> She served as executive officer of the American Physical Society<ref name="CSWP article"/> for 15 years,<ref name="judy franz blog">{{cite web|url=https://ggstem.wordpress.com/2013/06/04/judy-franz/|title=Judy Franz|last=Franz|first=Judy|date=2013-06-04|website=[[Grandma Got STEM]]}}</ref> encouraging more women to pursue careers in physics.<ref name="CSWP article"/> She is past Secretary General of the International Union of Pure and Applied Physics.<ref>{{Cite book|last=Council|first=National Research|url=https://www.nap.edu/catalog/13306/blueprint-for-the-future-framing-the-issues-of-women-in|title=Blueprint for the Future: Framing the Issues of Women in Science in a Global Context: Summary of a Workshop|date=2012-10-17|isbn=978-0-309-22519-9|language=en|doi=10.17226/13306 |bibcode=2012nap..book13306N }}</ref> She is now retired.<ref name="judy franz blog"/>
